entry.title: Sam's Club Iconography
entry.summary: An iconic membership
entry.content:
Autor(es): Forma & Co

An iconic membership


Sam’s Club Iconography

Sam’s Club is an American membership-only warehouse club chain owned by Walmart, offering a wide range of products and services at competitive prices.

Turner Duckworth, the agency behind its redesigned visual identity, commissioned us to develop a new corporate iconography system to extend and reinforce the brand’s visual language.



From Typography to Iconography

The new Sam’s Sans typeface, designed by Sharp Type, became the starting point for the development of the iconography system. Drawing on its formal characteristics, we translated its visual language into a set of functional symbols, using circular geometry and diamond-shaped details as distinctive elements.
The result is a family of bold, expressive icons that feels consistent with the typography and Sam’s Club’s new visual identity.


A 16×16 Grid System

The iconography system is built on a 16 × 16 pixel grid, with a 14 × 14 pixel live area and 1 pixel of padding.

This structure ensures consistency in proportions, visual weight, and details across the entire icon family. A 32 × 32 unit subgrid allows for subtle optical adjustments, ensuring clarity and legibility at small sizes.

A flexible and scalable system designed to perform consistently across the brand’s different touchpoints and applications.



Client: Sam’s Club
Identity: Turner Duckworth
Typography: Sharp Type
Iconography: Forma

entry.title: Hervanta series
entry.summary: In the midst of the uniform concrete apartment blocks of Hervanta, Finnish architects Raili and Reima Pietilä created an expressive counterpoint: the Hervanta Central Axis (Hervannan keskusakseli). Built in two phases in 1979 and 1989, this red-brick complex—comprising a community center, church, and library—forms the social and sculptural heart of the district. Focusing on the organic, jagged brick facades, deep arcades, and dramatic roof lines that break away from classic functionalism. Exploring how the Nordic light interacts with the rough texture and warm tones of the red brick. The series was taken in July 2026. entry.title: 紙罐圖鉴II QUNLE PKG. 2 / Brand Culture Journal Design
entry.summary: Although the medium is a book, we approached the design from the application level—how it appears at exhibitions and events, in peripheral materials, and in extended products for corporate gifting; how it conveys the professionalism of paper-can technology while also delivering the visual impact of a new brand image. All of this needed to be balanced.
entry.content:
Autor(es): SAYSOOO 自白

Although the medium is a book, we approached the design from the application level—how it appears at exhibitions and events, in peripheral materials, and in extended products for corporate gifting; how it conveys the professionalism of paper-can technology while also delivering the visual impact of a new brand image. All of this needed to be balanced.

紙罐圖鉴 II ｜QUNLE PKG. 2
Brand Culture Journal Design: 
Brand Output and 
Annual Compilation & Expression


Overview​​​​​​​

Qunle Packaging has long focused on composite solutions in the paper-can format. This is the second catalogue we have designed for Qunle, regrouping and integrating 20 industry categories and 380 products. The products themselves are the answer; what we needed to do was make this "diversity" and "possibility" more visible.

群乐包装长期专注纸罐形态的复合解决方案。这是我们为群乐设计的第二本图鉴，重新收录整合了2O个行业类别、38O个产品。产品本身就是答案，我们要做的，是让这份“多样化”和“可能性”被更好地看见。​​​​​​​
So rather than a catalogue per se, it is more like a fresh visual statement that Qunle Packaging puts forward at regular intervals, using it to open a dialogue with brand partners, consumers, and the market at large: what Qunle is doing now, and what kinds of products and services it can offer.

所以与其说这是一本图鉴，它更像是群乐包装每隔一段时间就会推出的一次全新视觉亮相，借由它和品牌方、消费者以及整个市场建立交流：群乐正在做什么，又能为大家提供什么样的产品与服务。
Although the medium is a book, we approached the design from the application level—how it appears at exhibitions and events, in peripheral materials, and in extended products for corporate gifting; how it conveys the professionalism of paper-can technology while also delivering the visual impact of a new brand image. All of this needed to be balanced.

虽然载体是一本书，但我们会从应用层面去考量设计需求——如在会展活动上的形象应用、周边物料、公司对外礼赠的延伸产品，如何体现纸罐技术的专业性，同时兼顾新形象视觉传播的亮点，也都需要平衡。​​​​​​​
We thought: since the whole book is about paper cans, why not let the design grow out of the paper can itself? We "flattened" the cylindrical paper can—text follows the curve of the can's rim onto its body, with the first and last characters drawing inward along the arc, so that the typography and layout on the flat page also carry the feel of the can's curved surface. The cover then became a stack of paper cans in different sizes, heights, and colors, their silhouettes overlapping front to back, with information partly hidden and partly revealed, appearing from large to small. At first glance it looks scattered and disorderly, but in fact the book title, industry categories, product and craft types, and other information each find their place inside a different can, waiting for the reader to seek them out.

我们想到，既然整本书讲的是纸罐，设计不如就从纸罐本身长出来。我们把圆筒状的纸罐“平面化”——文字沿着罐口弧度落在罐身上，字首字尾顺着弧面向内收，让平面上的文字和排版也带着纸罐的弧面感。于是封面就是一摞大小高低、颜色各异的纸罐，罐形轮廓前后交叠，信息被挡一点、露一点，由大到小呈现。乍看错落无序，其实书名、行业分类、产品工艺类型等信息都各自躲进了不同的罐身里，等着读者去翻找。
This language of the paper can continues onto the inner pages. The book is bound with a dust jacket and an exposed-spine text block. The first half combines text and images to cover the factory, the history of paper cans, and classic case studies; the second half is a product and craft catalogue organized into 20 industry chapters, presenting specific products and craft details. Each chapter's transition page uses three paper cans in varying lengths and spacing to create a visual interlude, so that wherever readers turn, they are still walking within the language of the paper can.

这种纸罐的语言也一路延续到内页。整本书是护封加露书脊内芯，前半部分讲工厂、纸罐历史和经典案例，后半部分按20个行业章节展开具体的产品与工艺图录。每章过渡页用三个纸罐做长短疏密的穿插，读者翻到哪儿，都还走在纸罐的语言里。
Using the paper can as the visual motif, the cylinder is "flattened".
text follows the can-opening curve with inward-tapering ends, while the cover stacks cans of varying sizes and heights, partially obscuring information so titles and categories hide within can bodies. Inside, a dust jacket and exposed spine frame the first half—factory, history, cases—and the second half's catalogue of 380 products across 20 industries, with three-can transition pages sustaining the language. The journal is both an annual compilation and Qunle's brand output, expressing the possibilities of paper-can packaging.

以纸罐为视觉母题，将圆筒“平面化”。
文字沿罐口弧度排布、首尾内收，封面以大小高低错落的纸罐交叠遮挡信息，书名与分类藏于罐身。内页护封加露书脊，前半讲工厂、历史与案例，后半按20个行业展开380个产品图录，过渡页以三罐穿插延续语言。刊物既是年度收编，也是群乐品牌输出与纸罐可能性的表达。

entry.title: 「B4DAWN」服装品牌设计|Clothing Brand identity
entry.summary: Proyecto por 阿祖不收手 NON STOP® con 26 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): 阿祖不收手 NON STOP®



Brand Background
B4DAWN，由 B4（Before 数字简写）与 DAWN（黎明）组合而成，释义为黎明之前。这是昼夜交替里至暗却最靠近光亮的区间，是所有蓄力者抵达曙光前的必经阶段。
品牌以此命名，构筑独属于同频群体的精神暗号，以数字简写的街头语言，承载社群共识，形成克制而有力量的品牌宣言：我们活在黎明之前，我们暂未被看见，但我们正在到来；至暗时刻，属于我们。 品牌致敬每一位蛰伏前行的奋斗者——创业者、艺术家、创作者、运动员，以及所有默默沉淀、等待破土的人。成功从不是瞬间的爆发，而是一段长久的潜行；在光芒降临之前，持续蓄力、耐心奔赴，正是B4DAWN所倡导的内核。 

品牌视觉以马为核心载体。马，象征不息奔行、奔赴远方、自强不息，代表对理想的持续追逐，暗含马到功成的美好期许。图形创意取奔跑的行者，头戴马头向前行进：周身沉于暗夜，步履不曾停歇，待到抵达终点，卸下马头，直面破晓晨光。行者未必知晓终点的确切坐标，却始终保持向前的姿态，永不停下奔赴的脚步，黑暗不是终点，而是黎明到来前，属于奔赴者的序章。

B4DAWN—a combination of "B4" (shorthand for "before") and "DAWN"—signifies the time just before daybreak. It is the interval between night and day—the darkest moment, yet the one closest to the light—a necessary phase for all those gathering their strength before reaching the dawn.
The brand takes its name from this concept, establishing a spiritual code for a like-minded community. Using the "street" vernacular of shorthand, it embodies a shared ethos—a brand manifesto that is both restrained and powerful: We live in the time before the dawn; we may not yet be seen, but we are on our way. The darkest hour belongs to us. The brand pays tribute to every striver currently lying low and forging ahead—entrepreneurs, artists, creators, athletes, and all those quietly honing their craft, waiting for the moment to break through. Success is never an instantaneous explosion, but rather a long, steady journey in the shadows. To keep gathering strength and patiently moving toward the light—this is the core philosophy championed by B4DAWN.
The brand’s visual identity centers on the motif of the horse—a symbol of ceaseless movement, a drive toward distant horizons, and an unyielding spirit of self-improvement. It represents the persistent pursuit of one’s ideals, carrying with it the hopeful aspiration of eventual triumph. The graphic design depicts a traveler in motion, wearing a horse’s head as they move forward. Though their body is immersed in the deep night, their stride never falters. Upon reaching the destination, they cast off the horse’s head to face the breaking dawn. The traveler may not know the exact coordinates of their final destination, yet they maintain a forward-leaning posture, never ceasing their journey. Darkness is not the end; it is merely the prologue for those who are on their way to the dawn.

entry.title: EARTH UNBOUND
entry.summary: Proyecto por Patrycja Makowska con 11 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Patrycja Makowska

EARTH UNBOUND
Iceland from Above


From above, the earth reveals a language written in rivers, shadows, and the last traces of winter.
Beneath the fading snow, a different landscape begins to emerge. Golden hills unfold into intricate patterns, 
dark rivers carve their winding paths through the valleys, and the low winter sun transforms the terrain 
into a canvas of ochre, silver, and blue.

Here, nature seems suspended between seasons. Winter has not yet surrendered, 
but the land is already revealing the shapes and textures concealed beneath its frozen surface.
From the quiet presence of horses crossing the pale hillsides to the delicate, almost calligraphic lines of rivers, 
every detail becomes part of a larger composition.
Seen from the sky, familiar landscapes lose their scale and become something else 
entirely — abstract paintings shaped by water, light, time, and the restless forces of the earth.

EARTH UNBOUND is a photographic exploration of this fleeting transformation, when the boundaries between winter and spring begin to dissolve, and the land reveals its hidden character.



An aerial photographic study of Iceland.

entry.title: Yearbook of Type #8
entry.summary: Proyecto por Slanted Publishers con 31 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Slanted Publishers

Yearbook of Type #8
History Edition

The eighth edition of the acclaimed Yearbook of Type series presents a curated overview of contemporary type design (2024–2026), with a focus on history and heritage. Building on the successful concept of previous volumes, it brings together high-quality typefaces from leading publishers, independent designers, and foundries worldwide—making it a valuable resource for type selection.

Each typeface is presented across three pages: a specimen spread showcasing its character, followed by a detailed profile with styles, weights, language support, OpenType features, and key information on designers and foundries. A comprehensive index ensures quick navigation. An accompanying online microsite provides access to all featured typefaces for browsing and purchasing, extending the book into a functional digital library. 

For designers, agencies, and typographers, Yearbook of Type #8 is both an inspiring catalog and a practical reference.

– Detailed presentation of 155 recent typefaces
– Ample background information
– Index of all 152 type designers and 95 foundries from 29 countries
– Explanation of all OpenType features
– An online microsite that directly links the typefaces to the foundries’ websites (from this edition, as well as editions 3 through 7)

entry.title: Genie Healthcare
entry.summary: Proyecto por Denormalized ™ con 11 imágenes.
entry.content:
Autor(es): Denormalized ™, Roman Myronov, Sam Tipikin


Problem

Genie had a product that worked and a brand that was still missing a piece. The app pulled scattered health data into one place and made sense of it, but the experience was purely functional — healthcare blue and green, a generic AI sphere, screens that delivered information without ever suggesting who was delivering it. The identity had no character yet, and the parts weren't connected: logo, symbol and motion existed separately rather than as a system. In a category people already avoid, that piece matters more than it would anywhere else. How Genie makes someone feel decides whether they open it at all — and that was the layer still to come.

Here is how it used to look


The logo 

Most marks in health tech look interchangeable, and the old Genie wordmark sat in the middle of that pack. Healthcare also limits how far a brand can move. People trust a health product with their bodies, so the mark had to stay trustworthy. We kept that weight and looked for one detail that would make it recognisable. 

The name gave us that detail. A genie is a jinn, and a jinn trails off into smoke. We drew that smoke into the descender of the g, so a single letter carries the story of the name. That order fits a brand whose magic works in the background. 

Sub-brands 

Genie won't stay one product. Rather than hand over a single lockup, we built a derivation framework: a fixed lockup structure and rules for how colour carries across variants, so any sub-brand reads as part of the same family without being redrawn. The team can add products and stay aligned with the master brand without coming back to us.



Colors+type

Genie came to us with a palette, a set of gradients and a serif typeface already in use across their app. They wanted all three kept. Our research raised the problem with that: nearly every healthcare brand runs on blue and green, and Genie's palette sat right among them.  So the brief turned into a question of approach. We couldn't swap the assets, so we had to change how the brand used them. The work that follows shows how we took the client's own colours, gradients and type and built something that stands apart from the category.
​​​​​​​


Creative strategy

Genie gives each user personalised insights and guidance about their own health. Most health apps present the same information to everyone. We repositioned Genie as a spotlight: it shows what matters for you right now and leaves the rest in the dark until you need it.

The lamp

A genie lives in a lamp, and a lamp throws light on one spot. That became the brand's visual metaphor. We based the lamp silhouettes on biological and organic forms, so they sit naturally next to anatomy, body imagery and the client's gradients.

Shape generator

The brand has to keep working after we hand it over. Genie's marketing and product teams will produce new material for years, so we built them a tool that generates brand visuals. It creates lamp shapes and gradient compositions within the system's rules, and the team can make new assets without redrawing anything or coming back to us.



Beyond the lamp

The lamp introduced the idea. The gradient approach behind it goes much further. The same technique can take the form of whatever the context calls for, from an organ to a metric to a person in motion, and still read as Genie. The brand gets one visual language that adapts to the subject instead of a fixed set of symbols.

The app

The app is the brand's main home. Here the gradients do real work: each one shapes itself around the data it shows, so the interface carries the same spotlight idea as the rest of the brand.
​​​​​​​

Character

Genie's assistant started as an abstract sphere, the same glowing blob most AI products use. It had no link to health or to the name. We rebuilt it around fire.

Fire already carries the meanings a health guide needs. People talk about fire in someone's eyes when they mean energy, and a fire in the soul when they mean strength. Fire is the warmth of a living body. Healers used it as the first antiseptic, and stage magicians still use it to hold an audience. It also closes the loop with the name: in folklore, jinns are made of smokeless fire.

The flame gives the character a face and a range of moods. It nudges, reassures, rests and thinks, and each state changes its colour and shape using the same gradients as the rest of the brand.  In the app, users interact with Genie directly, and it responds with the brand's motion and colour. We wanted that experience to feel pleasant without costing readability, so type, contrast and hierarchy follow the standards a healthcare product needs. The character went through the same check. The gradient flame loses its detail at small sizes, so we drew a simplified mini Genie: a flat shape with the same face that stays readable when small and holds strong contrast on any surface.

​​​​​​​
Genie 
Brand identity and product design for an AI health guide
